conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm inquiring about two of my children - Alex, who's 18, and Blake, who's 19.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm assessing Child Benefit eligibility for Alex (18) and Blake (19).

Since both children are over 16, their eligibility depends on whether they're in approved education or training. Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 if they stay in approved education or training.

**Are Alex and Blake currently in approved education or training?** (This could include things like A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs, or similar qualifications)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of them are in education at the moment. Alex actually started an apprenticeship in Northern Ireland, but Blake isn't doing any training or education right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I need to gather a bit more information to make a proper assessment.

**Regarding Alex's apprenticeship in Northern Ireland - do you know approximately how many hours per week Alex works as part of this apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of the exact hours, but it's a proper apprenticeship - I believe it's full-time work as part of the training program.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**First, let me ask about Blake - is Blake currently working in paid employment, and if so, do you know how many hours per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Blake isn't working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have a couple more questions to help determine eligibility.

**Has Blake registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services? And if so, did this happen within the last 20 weeks after leaving education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Blake hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Just to confirm a few final details:

**Do you live in the UK, and do both Alex and Blake live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK, but no - neither Alex nor Blake live with me anymore.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is an important detail.

**Are you making financial contributions towards Alex and Blake's upkeep?** (This could include things like money for food, clothes, pocket money, or contributions towards their accommodation - and would need to be at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment, which is £25.60 per week for the eldest child and £16.95 per week for additional children)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards their upkeep. For Alex, I contribute £30 a week - I help with clothes and other things they need. For Blake, I give £20 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**When did Alex start the apprenticeship - was it after they turned 16?**

And **when did Blake leave education or training - approximately how long ago was that?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, Alex started the apprenticeship after turning 16. 

As for Blake, they left education a while back now - it's been well over a year, probably close to two years ago.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for either Alex or Blake. Here's why:

**For Alex (age 18):**
Although you're making contributions of £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep (which would normally help maintain eligibility when a child lives elsewhere), Child Benefit stops when a child starts an apprenticeship. Since Alex has started an apprenticeship, your entitlement to Child Benefit for Alex has ended.

**For Blake (age 19):**
Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they remain in approved education or training. Blake is not currently in education, training, or working. While there is a provision for Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education if they register with a careers service or the armed services, Blake is now 19 and left education 1-2 years ago - well beyond this period. Unfortunately, despite your £20 weekly contributions towards Blake's upkeep, Blake doesn't meet the fundamental eligibility requirements.

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. If either of their circumstances change - for example, if Blake enters approved education or training - you may wish to contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss your situation.

However, the fact that Alex has started an apprenticeship means Child Benefit eligibility has ended, regardless of the contributions being made.
